title: Stock Market Today Live, October 21: Sensex down 550 pts, Nifty below 22,700; Eternal, Bajaj Fin lead losers - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates - Find here all the live updates related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 21st October 2026.

At 1.22 pm, the Nifty 50 was at 22,724.55, down 164.40 points or 0.72 per cent from its Monday close of 22,888.95, while the Sensex traded at 73,475.53, shedding 377.37 points or 0.51 per cent from 73,852.90.

Of 4,471 stocks traded on BSE, 3,397 declined and only 873 advanced, with 306 stocks hitting lower circuits against 112 in upper circuits. SBI Securities noted the frontline indices had “slipped below the lows of the previous two sessions” following the gap-up reversal.

Click here to track Jio Platforms IPO Day 1 Live Updates

IT stocks were the lone bright spot on an otherwise bruising day. Infosys gained 2.68 per cent to ₹1,161.00, Tech Mahindra advanced 2.66 per cent to ₹1,826.40, TCS rose 2.20 per cent to ₹2,515.10, and HCL Technologies added 1.57 per cent to ₹1,401.50. UltraTech Cement bucked sectoral weakness with a 1.62 per cent gain to ₹10,822.00. Every other major sectoral index was in the red, with auto the worst performer.

On the losing side, Bajaj Finance fell 3.39 per cent to ₹924.85, Eternal declined 3.26 per cent to ₹309.75, Eicher Motors dropped 3.05 per cent to ₹7,125.00, Trent lost 2.57 per cent to ₹2,817.30, and Adani Enterprises fell 2.54 per cent to ₹2,590.00. The Nifty Midcap 100 declined 1.7 per cent and Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 2.4 per cent, indicating that the selling was broader and deeper than headline index moves suggested.

Foreign investor selling, elevated crude oil prices and US bond yields remain headwinds, while domestic institutional inflows and selective buying could cushion declines. Market direction is likely to remain sensitive to Q2 earnings and sectoral trends.

HDFC Bank’s internal probe found evidence that two senior executives shared confidential business strategies and possible market-sensitive information with outsiders.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Gautam Adani and Tata's N Chandrasekaran before visiting Reliance's Jamnagar refinery, Vantara and clean-energy giga factories.

IOC, ‌the country's top refiner, had planned to source about 47% of its crude imports from ‌West Asia producers under annual deals on a free-on-board (FOB) ‌basis ⁠

LMW Limited reported a standalone net profit of ₹87.21 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, up from ₹45.14 crore a year earlier and ₹66.01 crore in the preceding quarter.

The company also approved capacity expansion through a new unit in Coimbatore.

Revenue from operations: ₹1,127.52 crore, up 45.3% year on year from ₹776.03 crore and 32.1% sequentially from ₹853.30 crore.

Total income: ₹1,153.47 crore, versus ₹815.38 crore a year earlier.

Profit before tax: ₹118.52 crore, more than doubling from ₹59.14 crore in Q2 FY26.

Net profit: ₹87.21 crore, up 93.2% year on year.

Earnings per share: ₹81.63, compared with ₹42.25 in the year-ago quarter.

Total expenses: ₹1,034.75 crore, up from ₹756.24 crore, led by higher material consumption of ₹730.38 crore.

Vipul Organics today announced the appointment of Mr. Tushar Jagtap as President – India & Subcontinent, Sales & Marketing, effective immediately. He will report directly to the Managing Director and Directors of the Company.

Mr. Jagtap brings over 30 years of extensive experience in sales leadership, business development, strategic market expansion, and commercial management within the chemicals, pigments, and coatings industries, with reputed organizations such as Archroma and Clariant Chemicals (now Sudarshan Colorants) and driven robust growth.

In his new role at Vipul Organics, Mr. Jagtap will lead the Sales & Marketing function for India and the Subcontinent, focusing sharply on business expansion, deepening customer engagement, driving market penetration, and achieving the company’s commercial objectives.

Khazanchi Jewellers Ltd received in-principle approvals from BSE and NSE to migrate from SME platform to main board, subject to compliance and submission of listing applications. The approvals, valid for 45 days, facilitate transition to the capital market segment, pending final approval and regulatory compliance, with NSE launching a new mobile app for further procedures.

Energy sales: 12,090 million units, up 33% YoY.

Power-supply revenue: Rs. 4,019 crore, up 45% YoY.

Power-supply EBITDA: Rs. 3,835 crore, up 51% YoY, with margin expanding to 92.0% from 90.5% a year earlier.

Cash profit: Rs. 1,951 crore, up 45% YoY.

Consolidated net profit: Rs. 747 crore, compared with Rs. 644 crore in Q2 FY26.

Operational renewable capacity: 20.8 GW, up 24% YoY; the company added 4,083 MW over the past year.

Battery storage: Installed 3.08 GWh in Q2, taking cumulative BESS capacity to 6.63 GWh

Goa Carbon informed stock exchanges about rectification orders increasing the tax refund for FY2010-11 from Rs. 76.15 lakh to Rs. 1.42 crore, with additional interest granted. The company is evaluating its legal options regarding a pending writ petition before the Bombay High Court, Goa bench, linked to these tax refunds.
